walkthroughs.body_html:
Forces & Newton's Laws — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Forces & Newton's Laws brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Forces & Newton's Laws.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: A 5 kg mass has resultant force 20 N. Its acceleration is:
options: 4 m/s²
100 m/s²
25 m/s²
15 m/s²

mcqs.q: On Earth, the weight of a 10 kg object (take g = 9.8) is:
If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means the vectors are parallel.
It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.

mcqs.q: If 6 workers take 8 hours to paint a wall, how long would 12 workers take (assuming they work at the same rate)?
options: 8 hours, because each worker still has to do the same job.
It means the vectors are parallel.
4 hours — this is inverse proportion: double the workers, halve the time.
16 hours, because doubling the workers doubles everything including the time.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between simple and compound interest?
options: It means the vectors are parallel.
Simple and compound interest give the same total — compound just uses a different formula.
Simple interest is calculated only on the original amount; compound interest is calculated on the original amount plus accumulated interest.
Simple interest grows faster than compound because it has fewer steps.
